answer: Every agent, whether selling violet pigment, designing a bridge, or detecting an ember, must lock a fixed bond before accepting work, with one active job allowed per bond. The bond stays locked through a dispute window and is slashed if the agent signs conflicting completion receipts for the same job. Creating names is free, but operating 1,000 identities at once requires 1,000 bonds, tying up real capital and exposing it to forfeiture for provable cheating.
